title: Do Deep Ensembles Actually Capture Uncertainty in Graph Neural Networks?
abstract: arXiv:2605.22593v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: While deep ensembles are widely considered to be the default method for uncertainty quantification in deep learning, their effectiveness for graph-structured data is often simply assumed based on successes in domains like computer vision. We investigate standard deep ensembles specifically for message-passing graph neural networks. Benchmarking across eight datasets representing varied tasks and complexities, we reveal that ensembles provide only marginal improvement over a single model. These marginal gains stem primarily from averaging out optimization noise in point predictions rather than from meaningfully better uncertainty estimates. Through an aleatoric-epistemic decomposition, we identify epistemic collapse: independently trained networks consistently converge to overly similar predictions. translated_title: 深度集成真的能捕获图神经网络中的不确定性吗？
translated_abstract: 尽管深度集成被广泛认为是深度学习中不确定性量化的默认方法，但其在图结构数据上的有效性往往仅是基于计算机视觉等领域取得的成功而简单假定的。我们专门针对消息传递图神经网络研究了标准深度集成方法。通过在八个代表不同任务和复杂度的数据集上进行基准测试，我们发现集成方法相较于单一模型仅能带来边际改进。这些边际收益主要源于对点预测中优化噪声的平均化消除，而非来自实质上更好的不确定性估计。通过偶然不确定性-认知不确定性的分解分析，我们识别出一种“认知坍缩”现象：独立训练的网络总是收敛到过于相似的预测。由于分歧是集成方法捕获认知不确定性的基本机制，这种多样性的缺失使得该方法失效（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 研究发现深度集成在图神经网络中并不能有效捕获认知不确定性，其边际改进仅来自平均化优化噪声，而独立训练的网络因“认知坍缩”现象收敛到过于相似的预测，缺乏集成方法所需的多样性。
en_tdlr: Deep ensembles provide only marginal gains over single models in GNN uncertainty quantification due to "epistemic collapse"—independently trained networks converge to overly similar predictions, eliminating the diversity needed to capture epistemic uncertainty.
